entry.title: Kafka producers on Amazon MSK: why retries=0 quietly turns off idempotence, and how to separate call latency from delivery timeout
entry.content: Teams with strict latency targets sometimes set retries=0 and shorten every producer timeout. On Amazon MSK this turns routine broker restarts, such as rolling patching, into failed sends. With default settings retries=0 also disables idempotence, leaving only an INFO log line. This article explains that behavior from the Kafka source, how max.block.ms, request.timeout.ms and delivery.timeout.ms relate, and a design that keeps latency targets.
entry.dc:creator: AWS re:Post Articles

entry.title: "Topic not present in metadata" on Amazon MSK when permissions are fine: idle topics, first sends, and max.block.ms
entry.content: This producer error means send() did not get topic metadata within max.block.ms, not that the topic is missing. Beyond missing DESCRIBE permission (covered in another re:Post article), it often hits the first send after a topic was idle longer than metadata.max.idle.ms, or the first send after start-up. This article explains why, how to read Kafka client logs to find the stalled stage, and how to warm up producers.
entry.dc:creator: AWS re:Post Articles

entry.title: Moving an Amazon MSK Connect connector to a new MSK cluster: why swapping a DNS alias is not enough

Data can then flow from the new cluster while the connector's framework state topics and worker connections stay on the old one, and deleting the old cluster drops the tasks. This article explains why, how to verify a connector has fully moved before deletion, and the supported migration path.
entry.dc:creator: AWS re:Post Articles

entry.title: Monitoring consumer lag on Amazon MSK: why time lag alone misses stalled consumers and raises false alarms
entry.content: EstimatedMaxTimeLag is documented as a time estimate to drain MaxOffsetLag, so it is derived from offset lag rather than measured on its own. As a result, a stalled consumer group on a low-throughput topic can show 0 seconds of time lag for hours, while a healthy group on a bursty topic can spike to hundreds of seconds. This article explains both patterns and gives reading and alarm rules that combine time lag with offset lag.
entry.dc:creator: AWS re:Post Articles

entry.title: Investigating repeated Kafka Streams rebalances on Amazon MSK when no member joined or left (probing rebalances)

This article covers where to get the client and broker logs on MSK, the log lines that confirm it, the defaults and lower bounds of probing.rebalance.interval.ms, acceptable.recovery.lag and max.warmup.replicas, why two of them must change together, and why the RebalanceInProgress metric does not answer this question.

entry.title: Why transaction.timeout.ms shows 10000 instead of 60000 in a Kafka Streams EOS application
entry.content: With processing.guarantee=exactly_once_v2, Kafka Streams overrides the producer transaction.timeout.ms to 10,000 ms (not the documented 60,000 ms) and commit.interval.ms to 100 ms. This article shows which values actually apply, why Streams changes them, how to confirm the effective values from the startup log, and the two constraints when you override them: startup fails if transaction.timeout.ms is below commit.interval.ms, and the broker's transaction.max.timeout.ms is the upper bound.
